_about: One definition of 'is this surface asking the person to choose?', shared by the runtime (runtime/app/fork.js::isDecisionDialog) and the compiler (conxa_compile/compiler/outcome_fork.py::classify_dialog). Both test suites load this file, so the two implementations cannot drift. A surface is a decision only when it has no input fields, is not a native dialog, is not a cookie/consent banner, has two or more buttons, and those buttons are not all plain dismiss labels. Anything else -- a toast, a progress panel, a lone Cancel -- is not. Each case also carries the surface `class` (notice | obstruction | decision_benign | info_request | decision_consequential | native) that fork.js::classifySurface and outcome_fork.py::classify_surface must agree on, and `irreversible_labels` pins is_irreversible_label / isIrreversibleLabel (a popup with an irreversible-looking button is never answered by an agent). `live` and `progress` are optional probe flags: a toast or progress panel is a notice. `blocks` and `stops_when_left_open` are runtime-only: `blocks` is the measured page_scripts.js::dialogProbe fact (true | false | null/absent = could not tell, counts as blocking) and `stops_when_left_open` is whether fork.js::isBlockingDecision ends a run that finished with this surface still open. Words never turn a decision into a notice; only a measured `blocks: false` lets a run carry on past one.
